claims.text: The initial material is a dense, nanocrystalline or fine-grained HEA coating on a transition-metal matrix.
AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 can have a microstructure containing multiple finely distributed BCC phases and an additional complex phase.
The proposed coating is characterized by high hardness and a single-phase or multiphase solid-solution structure.
Wear resistance initially improves as ambient temperature increases from room temperature to an intermediate range.
The elevated-temperature improvement in wear resistance is caused by formation of a protective oxide layer under atmospheric conditions.
The protective tribo-oxide reduces direct metal-to-metal contact.
The coefficient of friction decreases slightly with increasing temperature.
Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni alloys exhibit temperature-dependent chemical clustering and high-temperature short-range ordering.
Increasing temperature causes a transition from dislocation-mediated plasticity to thermo-plastic instability in the proposed coating.
Thermo-plastic instability in Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni systems leads to lattice softening and loss of structural integrity.
Microstructural coarsening or phase instability will dominate at sufficiently high temperature.
High-temperature instability causes loss of hardness and rapid wear.
Specific wear rate reaches a minimum, corresponding to peak wear resistance, at approximately 400-600 °C.
Above the intermediate optimum, the wear rate rises sharply because the protective oxide breaks down and thermo-plastic instability begins.
At room temperature, the same HEA system has higher friction and wear because a fully developed protective tribo-oxide is absent.
The degradation boundary occurs when oxide formation can no longer compensate for thermal softening and matrix instability.
For Al-containing HEAs, performance degradation is expected above approximately 600-700 °C.
For refractory HEAs, performance degradation is expected above approximately 800 °C.
Refractory HEAs can retain high phase stability and substantial strength above 800 °C.
The degradation threshold and protective-oxide composition depend strongly on HEA composition and the transition-metal matrix.

contradictions.description: The falsification rule says that degradation in air but no degradation in inert gas would suggest a purely thermal-softening mechanism. The opposite inference follows: an atmosphere-dependent difference would implicate oxidation or oxide stability, whereas purely thermal softening should also occur in inert gas.
